newsitem.title: GERMANY: Moody's - negative long-term outlook for Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Moody's - negative long-term outlook for Dresdner.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday it was leaving unchanged its Aaa rating on the senior unsecured debt of German bank Dresdner Bank AG but has negative long-term and financial strength ratings.
Moody's said the existing rating was based on Dresdner's "superior creditworthiness".
"We continue to view Dresdner as a very strong and financially stable banking group both by German and international standards," Moody's said in a statement.
But it added, "The outlook for the long-term and financial strength ratings are negative."

Moody's said the outlook incorporated the belief that the European banking market will put Dresdner's traditional revenue source, mainly net lending margins, "under continuous downward pressure, thus challenging the group's earnings power".
The report noted that the European market was currently characterised by low loan demand, tighter margins, increasing product commoditisation and gradual savings disintermediation.

To offset the trend, Moody's said Dresdner was pursuing a strategy of diversifying its earnings sources, both domestically and internationally, through fees and commissions and also through trading income (not from proprietary trading).
The report also said the integration of U.K. investment bank Kleinworth Benson was going on but that Dresdner faced stiff competition.
"Dresdner is also making sustained efforts to improve the efficiency of its domestic network, but the overall cost structure remains a financial burden," the report said.
Moody's also said disclosed solvency was not very high at Dresdner by international standards but that Dresdner's economic capitalisation was boosted by hidden reserves.
